title: Consultancy to Develop Learning Paper 2 for SPREAD- Integrating Peacebuilding, Livelihoods, Climate Resilience and Disaster Risk Reduction

# Work Plan

## Narrative

Cortech Consulting Group will deliver the SPREAD Learning Paper 2 assignment over the 12-week period specified in the Terms of Reference, from on-boarding on 29 September 2026 through submission of the final learning paper and policy briefs on 15 December 2026.
The work plan is sequenced around the fixed dates the Terms of Reference set: inception report and tools approved by 13 October 2026, data collection to 31 October 2026, draft report to DCA by 21 November 2026, cross-border validation workshop by 3 December 2026, and final report and policy briefs by 15 December 2026.
Lead Consultant Mugove Kwashirai Chakurira will hold overall responsibility for methodology, analysis and reporting, reporting to the Project Consortium Manager with technical oversight from the SPREAD thematic leads and MEAL team.
Research Assistant Edwin Aldrin Adenya will support field enumeration and, per the administrative provisions of the Terms of Reference, the consultant will recruit and train additional local research assistants for Turkana/Kenya, South Omo/Ethiopia and Eastern Equatoria/South Sudan, coordinated through TUPADO (Kenya), ICPDO and ROG (South Sudan) and ECC (Ethiopia) using harmonised tools to ensure cross-country comparability.
## Phase Breakdown

**Phase 1: Inception (Week 1-2, 29 September to 13 October 2026).** Desk review of the SPREAD baseline report (2024), Mid-Term Review (2025), Year 3/MTR reflection workshop outputs, DCA's Conflict Prevention and Social Cohesion Action Guides, the Social Cohesion Index tool, and DCA's resilience, climate adaptation, DRR and Market Systems Development guidance.
Development of case-study selection criteria, KII/FGD guides and the community case-study protocol in consultation with SPREAD technical and MEAL staff.
Output: inception report covering desk review findings, methodology, sampling, tools, work plan and ethical/risk mitigation measures, presented at an inception briefing with the Consortium Management Unit (CMU) and thematic leads.
**Phase 2: Field Data Collection (Week 3-5, 14 to 31 October 2026).** Direct engagement with pastoralists/agro-pastoralists, fisherfolk, women- and youth-led CSOs, traditional leaders, local and national authorities, Community Action Group (CAG) and Village Savings and Loan Association (VSLA) members across all three countries, sequenced through TUPADO, ICPDO/ROG and ECC.
Output: completed KIIs, FGDs, participatory ranking exercises and community case studies covering livestock, fishing, farming and informal cross-border trade (ICBT), disaggregated by sex, age and disability.
**Phase 3: Analysis and Draft Reporting (Week 6-8, 1 to 21 November 2026).** Data cleaning, triangulation against SPREAD baseline and MTR findings, and a review session with the SPREAD team to deepen understanding of findings.
Output: draft learning paper and draft policy briefs (general integration brief and the human security/stability brief) submitted to DCA by 21 November 2026.
**Phase 4: Validation (Week 9, 22 November to 3 December 2026).** Preparation and circulation of validation materials, followed by the single cross-border validation workshop with Consortium members, IGAD and other stakeholders.
Output: validation workshop proceedings and feedback log.
**Phase 5: Finalization and Dissemination (Week 10-12, 4 to 15 December 2026).** Incorporation of validation feedback into the final learning paper, both policy briefs, executive management summary, summary PowerPoint, and anonymised case-study files and cleaned raw data.
Output: final deliverables submitted by 15 December 2026, followed by the facilitated results presentation and learning session with DCA and consortium partners.
## Parallel vs Sequential Activities

Inception, data collection, drafting and validation are sequential and gated: data collection begins only once the inception report and tools are approved (13 October), and validation begins only once the draft report is submitted (21 November).
Within Phase 2, data collection in Kenya, Ethiopia and South Sudan runs in parallel through the three national partner teams to meet the 31 October deadline.
Within Phase 5, drafting of the two policy briefs, the executive summary and the PowerPoint proceeds in parallel once validation feedback is received, converging on the single 15 December submission.

METHODOLOGY

1. Overall Approach

Cortech Consulting Group proposes a learning-focused, mixed-methods design that treats "integration" as the central unit of analysis, not a background descriptor. SPREAD is now in its third year of implementation and moving toward its concluding phase; the assignment is therefore not a standard evaluation of outputs but a structured process of extracting operational meaning from three years of programme experience across Turkana/Kenya, South Omo/Ethiopia and Eastern Equatoria/South Sudan, the Karamoja Cluster cross-border zone. The methodology is designed to answer directly what the Terms of Reference itself asks: what integration has meant operationally in SPREAD's design and inception, when it has added value beyond the sum of Peacebuilding, Livelihoods, Climate Resilience and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) delivered in parallel, what trade-offs this has produced, and what this implies for future funding and programming models. The design combines document-based reconstruction of SPREAD's integration logic with field-based testing of that logic against lived community experience. It builds explicitly on SPREAD's existing Outcome Harvesting practice rather than introducing a parallel evaluative framework, and it is structured around community case studies that will deliberately include both stronger and weaker examples of integration, as required by the ToR, so that the paper can explain contextual variation rather than assert a single success narrative. The methodology is anchored on four analytical moves that map directly to the six proposed key learning questions: (i) establishing a shared operational definition of integration through desk review and stakeholder engagement; (ii) mapping sequencing patterns, including whether peace preceded livelihood investment, whether economic cooperation opened space for dialogue, or whether natural-resource agreements preceded irrigation or agricultural investment; (iii) surfacing challenges and trade-offs, including the relationship between livelihoods diversification and reduced pressure on natural resources; and (iv) assessing how communities relate to SPREAD-introduced structures, Community Action Groups (CAGs), Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs), micro-grants and early warning systems, alongside pre-existing structures such as market committees, peace committees and savings groups. 2. Phase-by-Phase Breakdown

Phase 1, Inception (weeks 1 to 2, targeting the 13 October 2026 milestone). This review will produce a working operational definition of integration and a first map of sequencing hypotheses to be tested in the field. In parallel, the consultant will develop case-study selection criteria, KII and FGD guides, and a community case-study protocol in consultation with SPREAD technical and MEAL staff, satisfying Expected Task 2 of the ToR. All instruments will be piloted in KoboToolbox before use. Phase 2, Field Data Collection (October, through 31 October 2026). Data collection will be coordinated across the three countries through the national partner teams, TUPADO in Kenya, ICPDO and ROG in South Sudan, and ECC in Ethiopia, using harmonised Kobo tools to preserve cross-country comparability. Edwin Aldrin Adenya, supported by locally recruited research assistants trained by the Lead Consultant, will support enumeration and FGD/KII facilitation in line with the ToR's administrative provision that the consultant recruit and train research assistants directly. Phase 3, Analysis and Quality Review (early to mid-November 2026). Qualitative data (KII and FGD transcripts, case-study narratives) will be coded in NVivo against a codebook built around the four analytical moves above. Quantitative and ranking-exercise data will be cleaned and analysed in SPSS, disaggregated by sex, age and disability. A dedicated review session with the SPREAD team, satisfying Expected Task 4, will be held to deepen understanding of emerging findings before drafting begins. Phase 4, Reporting and Validation (21 November to 15 December 2026). A draft learning paper and draft policy briefs will be prepared and discussed with the Consortium Management Unit (CMU) and relevant thematic leads, followed by a single cross-border validation workshop bringing together Consortium members, IGAD and other stakeholders, and a final revision cycle incorporating validation feedback. 3. Method by Deliverable

Inception Report (13 October 2026). Instrument: structured desk review matrix plus draft KII/FGD guides and case-study protocol. Respondents: SPREAD CMU and thematic leads (consultation only, no primary data). Output: inception report covering desk review findings, methodology, case-study selection criteria, data collection tools, work plan and ethical/risk mitigation measures, presented at an inception briefing. Field Data Collection. Instruments: KIIs with traditional leaders, local and national authorities, and private-sector actors; FGDs with CAG and VSLA members, farmers and farmer groups, fisherfolk, and women- and youth-led CSOs; participatory ranking exercises with mixed and women/youth-led markets. Sampling will span all three countries and cover peacebuilding and resilience structures, livestock, fishing, farming and formal and informal cross-border trade (ICBT). Output: cleaned Kobo datasets and case-study narrative files per country. Draft and Final Learning Paper. Instrument: triangulated analysis across NVivo-coded qualitative data, SPSS-analysed ranking and disaggregated data, and the Phase 1 desk review, structured around the six key learning questions. Output: draft learning paper (21 November 2026) and final learning paper with SMART, evidence-based recommendations on integration versus coordination (15 December 2026). Policy Briefs. Two distinct products, as specified in the ToR: a concise general policy brief on integration for donors, IGAD and governments, and a separate 4 to 8 page brief targeted at EU, Danish and IGAD policymakers on how the integrated approach contributes to human security and stability.
